facts.title: The Great Wall of China
facts.text: It is thousands of kilometres long. Different Chinese dynasties built and rebuilt it over about 2,000 years to protect their lands.

facts.title: The Great Pyramid
facts.text: The ancient Egyptians built the Great Pyramid of Giza about 4,500 years ago, using millions of huge stone blocks and no machines.

facts.title: Paper comes from China
facts.text: Paper was invented in ancient China about 2,000 years ago. Around the year 105, an official named Cai Lun (蔡伦) made papermaking much better.

facts.title: Singapore's birthday
facts.text: Singapore became an independent country on 9 August 1965. That is why National Day is celebrated on 9 August every year.

facts.title: Raffles arrives
facts.text: In 1819, Sir Stamford Raffles arrived in Singapore and set up a British trading port. It grew into a busy port city.

facts.title: People on the Moon
facts.text: In 1969, the Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first people to walk on the Moon.

facts.title: The first aeroplane flight
facts.text: In 1903, the Wright brothers flew the first powered aeroplane. The first flight lasted only 12 seconds!

facts.title: The first Olympics
facts.text: The Olympic Games began in ancient Greece more than 2,700 years ago. The modern Olympics started again in 1896.

facts.title: Dinosaurs
facts.text: Dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago, long, long before the first humans lived.

facts.title: The Terracotta Army
facts.text: Thousands of life-size clay soldiers were made for China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang (秦始皇), more than 2,200 years ago.

facts.title: Movable type printing
facts.text: Around the year 1040, Bi Sheng (毕昇) in China invented movable type: single characters that could be arranged to print pages.

facts.title: The compass
facts.text: The magnetic compass was invented in ancient China. Later, sailors used it to find their way across the oceans.

facts.title: Gutenberg's printing press
facts.text: Around 1440, Johannes Gutenberg in Germany built a printing press that made books much faster and cheaper to make.

facts.title: The first telephone
facts.text: In 1876, Alexander Graham Bell made one of the first telephone calls. Now we carry phones in our pockets!
